overview.title: Welcome to Taroudant — Little Marrakech of the Souss
overview.p1: Taroudant sits in the Souss plain behind long ochre ramparts. Travellers nickname it the Little Marrakech for its walls and medina — without the imperial-city intensity. Place Assarag organises daily life; the souks and gates reward slow walking.
overview.p2: One full day covers the walls, Assarag and the markets; a second morning suits Tioute or a deeper medina wander. Stay inside or near the walls for atmosphere, or use Taroudant as a calmer base in the Souss.

q1.question: How many days should I spend in Taroudant?
q1.answer: One full day covers the ramparts, Assarag and the souks. A second day allows you to visit Tioute oasis or explore the medina at a slower pace.

q2.question: Why is it called Little Marrakech?
q2.answer: Because of its massive continuous red-ochre ramparts and bustling medina atmosphere, mirroring Marrakech but in a much more relaxed Souss setting.

q3.question: How do I get to Taroudant?
q3.answer: Most travelers arrive by road from Agadir (about 1.5 to 2 hours) or via the mountain roads from Marrakech.

q4.question: Best time to visit?
q4.answer: Spring and autumn. Summer is very hot on open ramparts; winter is mild by day and cool at night.
